counterfactual_missing_items: No CD56 or EBV status to further classify the T/NK-cell lymphoma
No T-cell receptor gene rearrangement study
No explicit hemophagocytosis on biopsy to confirm secondary HLH
decisive_items: Third Bone Marrow Biopsy: Near-total effacement of marrow by necrotic, high-grade tumor
Immunohistochemistry: Positive for CD2, cytoplasmic CD3, CD30, perforin, TIA-1; Negative for CD4, CD5, CD7, CD8, TCR-gamma, ALK-1
response.rationale: C1 is the most complete fixed candidate: it preserves the T-cell lineage established by IHC and adds the histologic grade explicitly stated in the third marrow biopsy. R4 is the same diagnosis without the grade modifier. R1 captures the secondary HLH-like laboratory picture but lacks the definitive tissue diagnosis and is better explained as a complication of the underlying high-grade T-cell lymphoma.

rejected.why: Fever, hyperferritinemia, and cytopenias are nonspecific and can be secondary to the underlying lymphoma; no hemophagocytosis is described and the marrow/IHC findings establish a high-grade T-cell lymphoma.
